every-line-of-a-loaded-skill-is-a-recurr.description: Once loaded, a skill's content "stays in context across turns, so every line is a recurring token cost" [1], and every token "competes for the agent's attention" [2].

a-home-for-each-fact.title: A home for each fact
a-home-for-each-fact.script: Take one piece of project knowledge, something that changes from one project to the next, like the depth of today's dive site. It needs a home, and you have to pick one. Choosing where each piece of context lives is information architecture, the same craft that decides where things go on a well-built website, and you practise it whether or not you call it that.

three-costs.title: Three costs
three-costs.script: Every home costs you in three ways. Performance asks whether the model actually reads it at the moment it needs it, reusability asks how many projects the skill still fits, and token cost asks how much of the context window it fills, and how often.

three-homes.title: Three homes
three-homes.script: There are three homes for it. Inside the skill, it arrives every time the skill runs, but now the skill fits only this project. In your project instructions, it sits in the context window on every task, whether the task needs it or not, and the skill stays free for any project. In a project file the skill reads, it is loaded only at the step that needs it, and the skill fits every project. None is right in general, so it depends on how many projects the skill will serve.
